messages:
maya: Heads-up — got 3 customers reporting alerts that fired at 03:00 UTC even though the dashboard shows empty bars for the metric. Alert history shows a single high data point at the boundary then nothing. Anyone seen this before?

jonathan: saw one earlier. looks like the aggregation window might be getting truncated to a few seconds at the rollup boundary. can you paste the chart link + the alert query?

maya: https://console.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/request-rate - alert config: eval_window=1m, threshold=5rps, source metric=requests.count(1m). chart shows 0 points for the 03:00 bucket but the alert fired at 03:00:01. no deploys on those customers.

kevin: thanks. two likely causes: 1) rollup job alignment bug where the last bucket becomes shorter during compaction/retention window, leading to an inflated per-second rate after normalization, or 2) a timezone/epoch alignment mismatch where we floor windows differently between chart and alert eval.

kevin: quick repro to check: run the raw query over the exact window endpoints and compare bucket durations. eg:```sql
SELECT count(*) as c, min(ts) as start_ts, max(ts) as end_ts, (end_ts-start_ts) as duration_s
FROM requests
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-16T02:59:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-16T03:01:00Z'
GROUP BY time_bucket('60s', ts, '1970-01-01 00:00:00+00')
```

maya: ran that — the 03:00 bucket duration shows 5s for one tenant (end-start = 5). that explains the spike after dividing by seconds.

ash: confirmed in rollup logs: compaction ran at 03:00:00 and we had a race where cleanup truncated the active bucket before the eval job finished. root cause: rollup worker A committed a partial bucket when worker B took over, leaving a short bucket.

ash: created a hotfix branch fix/rollup-window-alignment — it enforces atomic commit of active buckets and aligns bucket boundaries to the global epoch offset. planning a canary deploy to eng-runtime staging now.

kevin: mitigation for support — increase alert eval_window to 3m or set evaluation_periods: 2 so single-bucket truncation doesn't fire a page. also we can add a temporary rule to ignore buckets with duration < 30s.

maya: doing that for the affected customers now. can you also add a dashboard widget that shows bucket duration so support can triage quickly?

ash: yes, adding a small metric (rollup.bucket_duration_seconds) and a per-tenant heatmap. will post PR link.

support-bot: Ticket #SR-2026-589 created for tracking (assignee: ash). linked to customer cases C-4212, C-4218, C-4220.

jonathan: once canary is green, schedule a patch release to prod. also add an alert on abnormal bucket durations (> 2x baseline) so we catch regressions.

maya: great — thanks everyone. customers notified and we've paused noisy alerts. :thumbsup:
